question: What is the molecular mass of an ozone molecule?
solution:
The correct answer is __**48**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular formula of ozone is **O₃**, which means it consists of three oxygen atoms.
 
• The atomic mass of one oxygen atom (O) is approximately **16 atomic mass units (amu)**.
 
• To find the molecular mass of ozone (O₃), we need to sum the atomic masses of all the oxygen atoms present in the molecule: **3 * 16 amu = 48 amu**.
 
• Hence, the molecular mass of an ozone molecule is **48 amu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Mass:**

 
 
• Molecular mass (or molecular weight) is the mass of a given molecule, calculated as the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the molecule.
 
• It is usually expressed in atomic mass units (amu) or Daltons (Da).
 
• For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) is calculated as 2*(1 amu) + 16 amu = 18 amu.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The atomic mass of an element is the mass of a single atom of the element, typically expressed in atomic mass units (amu).
 
• It is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom (the mass number).
 
• For example, the atomic mass of carbon is approximately 12 amu.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃):**
 
 
• Ozone is a molecule composed of three oxygen atoms.
 
• It is a highly reactive and unstable form of oxygen, with a strong oxidizing ability.
 
• Ozone is found naturally in the Earth's stratosphere and forms the ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.
